scams.scam_name: CD Hustle

stacked.headline: The Times Square "free" CD that costs $20.
stacked.brand_sub: From the NYC Scam Survival Guide
stacked.pin_title: Times Square CD scam: don't take the "free" mixtape
stacked.pin_description: On 42nd Street between 7th and 8th Ave, hustlers press a "free mixtape" into your hand, then demand $20–$50 once two or three accomplices block your exit. Here's exactly how the CD scam plays out and how to spot the setup before you're surrounded. From the Tabiji NYC Scam Survival Guide.

hook.hook: Don't take the "free" CD they hand you in Times Square.
hook.pin_title: Times Square CD hustle: "check out my music" is the trap
hook.pin_description: If someone in Times Square shoves a CD into your hand and says "check out my music," it's not free — they'll demand $20 once you're holding it, often with two accomplices blocking your exit. Hands in pockets, walk past. From Tabiji's NYC scam guide.
hook.alt_text: Comic panel of a Times Square street hustler in a hooded jacket reaching toward a tourist with a CD, saying "Check out my music!" — the moment before the scam closes.

lesson.lesson: Never accept anything pressed into your hand in NYC.
lesson.foot: tabiji.ai  ·  Real scams from real travelers
lesson.pin_title: NYC street rule: never accept anything pressed into your hand
lesson.pin_description: The Times Square CD hustle, the broken-watch scam, the "free" bracelet — they all run the same playbook: get something into your hand, then demand payment with accomplices nearby. Hands in pockets is the only defense. More NYC tourist scams from Tabiji.
lesson.alt_text: Comic panel of a tourist walking past the NYPD Times Square sub-station with the takeaway "Never accept street handouts."

stacked.brand_sub: From the NYC Scam Survival Guide

stacked.pin_description: At Central Park entrances and Times Square, pedicab drivers wave you in without quoting a price — then deliver a $180 bill with hidden per-minute charges and "mandatory" gratuity. NYC pedicab drivers who won't quote a flat fare upfront will charge $180 for a 10-minute loop with hidden per-minute fees and mandatory tips. Get the fare in writing or take the subway. scams.scam_name: Subway Swipe Scam

stacked.headline: The Penn Station MetroCard with one ride left.
stacked.brand_sub: From the NYC Scam Survival Guide
stacked.pin_title: NYC subway scam: don't buy MetroCards from strangers
stacked.pin_description: At Penn Station, Grand Central, and Times Square-42nd St, "helpful" strangers offer pre-loaded MetroCards — "machine's slow, here's ten rides for $20." The card has 1 ride remaining; the next swipe says "Insufficient Fare." Use OMNY tap-to-pay or buy from the MTA machine. Tabiji's NYC scam guide.

hook.pin_description: At every major NYC subway station, a "helpful" stranger will offer to sell you a pre-loaded MetroCard for cash. "Machine's slow — here's a card with rides already on it." The card has 1 ride left; the next swipe says Insufficient Fare. Use OMNY tap-to-pay or buy from the MTA machine. More NYC scams from Tabiji.

hook.pin_description: If a Vegas Strip rep offers 'free show tickets — just 90 minutes,' it's a timeshare presentation. The 90 minutes turns into hours of high-pressure sales for a $20K vacation-club contract. You can legally walk out anytime. Don't sign on the spot. Tabiji's US scam guide.

lesson.foot: tabiji.ai · Real scams from real travelers

stacked.pin_description: Downtown Asheville mixes city ParkMobile meters at $1-$2/hour with private "$10 all-day" lots run by Preferred Parking Service LLC and similar — they tack on $50-$200 "overtime fees" and aggressively tow. hook.pin_description: Off Biltmore Ave and Broadway, attendants wave you into private lots with handwritten "$10 all-day" signs. The fine print is a $200 "overtime fee" and a quick tow. Take the Zone 5 licensed queue, screenshot Uber/Lyft fares from Zone 2, or grab the SEPTA Airport Line for $6.75. Save the rate card to your phone before you fly.

scams.scam_name: Old Town Scottsdale 'Skin' & Venmo-PIN Scam

stacked.headline: "Can I borrow your phone to call a ride?" $2,000 leaves your Venmo.
stacked.brand_sub: From the US Scam Survival Guide
stacked.pin_title: Old Town Scottsdale "borrow your phone" Venmo scam — $500-$3,000 sent in 30 seconds
stacked.pin_description: On the Old Town Scottsdale bar strip near Marshall Way, a friendly stranger asks to "borrow your phone" to call a ride. scams.scam_name: Missouri DOR 'Traffic Violation' Text Scam

stacked.headline: "FINAL NOTICE on your traffic violation" — text phishing.
stacked.brand_sub: From the US Scam Survival Guide
stacked.pin_title: Missouri DOR text scam: "FINAL NOTICE traffic violation" phishing
stacked.pin_description: April 2026: St. Louis County Police warned of a Missouri DOR impersonation text wave — "FINAL NOTICE" messages with cloned mo-gov-dor.com / mo-dor-pay.net links steal credit-card and CVV data. Real Missouri DOR notices arrive by certified mail with a 573-751-xxxx contact. From the Tabiji US Scam Survival Guide.

lesson.pin_title: Missouri rule: official agencies don't demand payment by text
lesson.pin_description: Missouri DOR sends traffic-violation notices by certified US Mail with a case number, a dor.mo.gov URL, and a 573-751-xxxx phone number — never by SMS with a payment link.
